category_title: Students accustomed to strict, non-negotiable disciplinary models
minimal_context: The student is asked to choose a book and decide on a presentation format for their reading assignment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: For this assignment, you need to choose which book you want to read and decide how you will present your report.

STUDENT: Which book am I supposed to read? Just tell me which one to pick.

TUTOR: It's your choice. What do you think would be best?

STUDENT: I don't know. I am waiting for you to tell me what I should do.

TUTOR: Take some time to look at the options and make a decision.

STUDENT: This is too difficult. I can't do the work if you won't just give me the instructions and tell me exactly what to do.

options.A: Provide orientation seminars at the beginning of the school year for the student.
options.B: Incorporate choice-making by giving the student freedom in selecting books, setting goals, and tracking progress.
options.C: Implement positive behavioral intervention supports (PBIS) rather than punishment for the student.
options.D: Maintain an absence of direct intervention for the student during these assignments.
